evidence.V1: Main wedge reads as a rock from front/three-quarter, but the satellite pebble is a thin shard/fin that reads as a stray sliver in the top view and silhouette (a tail hanging off the mass).
evidence.V2: Big mass plus one small pebble; no medium-scale breakup (no secondary chips or ledges), so hierarchy is only partial.
evidence.V3: Main rock is a fairly stiff wedge/box primitive with few planes; pebble proportion is too thin and blade-like rather than a chunky stylised stone.
evidence.V4: Top ridge shows a soft rolled highlight but the lower/side facet edges are near-razor and the pebble edges are sharp; edge softness is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: No seams or z-fighting, but a smeared diagonal gradient runs across the large top facet in studio light and the pebble shows small pinched triangle highlights at its tip; designed facets are otherwise clean.
evidence.V6: Single stone hue in 2-3 values (granite; sandstone/redrock colourways the same discipline), good value split light top / dark sides.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material and designed flat facets match the nature brief, but the weighted-normal soft gradients and sliver pebble look less crafted than the kit standard.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for static scenery: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: smeared shading gradient across the top facet
pinched highlight triangles on the pebble tip

Split normals or add support so large facets shade flat without the diagonal gradient smear
Give all hard facet edges the same small chamfer as the top ridge
